hook: A 1948 administrative compilation from USAF Intelligence Directorate routing flying disc sighting reports and Horten Brothers aircraft investigation memos to Air Materiel Command at Wright-Patterson, spanning January through June 1948 under Project SIGN.
why_it_matters: This file captures the early bureaucratic machinery of Project SIGN in operation, showing how flying disc reports from FBI field agents, foreign military attachés, and Air Force field commands were centrally collected by USAF Intelligence and forwarded to Wright-Patterson for technical analysis. The explicit investigation of German Horten Brothers flying wing designs as a possible explanation for disc sightings — including direct military interrogation of the Horten Brothers themselves — reveals one of the primary conventional hypotheses being actively pursued in 1948. The multi-agency scope, spanning domestic witnesses, FBI, Canadian and Soviet military attachés, demonstrates that SIGN was drawing on the full intelligence apparatus.

key_findings.finding: Railway workers in Hobson, Ohio on the night of 8 May 1948 reported a round, phosphorescent object approximately nine inches in apparent diameter from ground level, traveling at great speed at altitude of 5–6 miles on a 90-degree heading and leaving a phosphorescent trail. The report reached USAF via FBI Special Agent D.K. Brown of Cleveland.

key_findings.finding: The Air Force was actively investigating whether German Horten Brothers flying wing designs explained flying disc sightings. A classified T-2 technical report on the subject was retained by USAF Intelligence, and the European Command's G2 was directed via telecon to interrogate the Horten Brothers directly using Collection Memorandum Number 7 as the basis.

key_findings.finding: Project SIGN served as the explicit administrative and filing framework for all flying disc correspondence routed through USAF Intelligence to Wright-Patterson, with multiple routing forms directly naming it.

Flying disc reporting was governed by a formal USAF directive dated 6 February 1948 requiring all commands to forward sighting information to Washington and AMC, with distribution copies to Air Defense Command — establishing a mandatory multi-echelon reporting chain from field units to Wright-Patterson.

key_findings.finding: Foreign military intelligence was integrated into the flying disc investigation: a U.S. Military Attaché report from Moscow referenced 1400 aircraft, and a Canadian Military Air Attaché report was used to formally close a specific incident involving individuals named Johnson and Harrison.

legacy_program_connections.reasoning: Multiple routing forms and correspondence reference forms explicitly name Project SIGN as the filing framework, making this a direct administrative record of SIGN's operation — the immediate predecessor to Project Blue Book.
Air Materiel Command at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base is the designated recipient of every forwarded flying disc report and investigation memo in this file, identified by office symbol TSDIN/MCI.

A Canadian Military Air Attaché report was formally incorporated into the investigation to close the Johnson-Harrison incident, indicating allied intelligence sharing on flying disc cases in early 1948.
Collection Memorandum Number 7 and the Moscow military attaché report indicate active foreign intelligence collection on the flying disc question running parallel to domestic SIGN operations.
